comments.author: sgentle
comments.story_title: Ask HN: I feel like I should be working all the time and its killing me
comments.why_zh: Hickey 是对抗持续工作焦虑的一剂解药。
comments.quote_zh: 我会把你引向我最喜欢的两位 Richard。
comments.text_zh: 你描述的那种感觉叫焦虑。有些焦虑是正常的，但持续焦虑并干扰你的生活就是个问题。我觉得值得试试这个标签：把它叫作焦虑，然后问“我该怎么减轻我的焦虑？”大约每 4 个人中就有 1 人在一生中的某个时刻经历焦虑障碍，所以这方面的研究和好方法有很多。让我注意到的一点是，你提出了一些相当重大又吓人的论断，却没有多少证据支持。你真的不是一名好开发者吗？聪明人真的在“抢占”机会吗（也就是随着时间推移机会变少）？那些不一直工作的人真的会落后，并且永远做不出什么重要成就吗？如果是这样，证明它！弄清楚你需要什么证据才能明确回答这些问题，然后去研究或实验，直到你拿到那些证据。焦虑的想法就像梦：在你脑子里显得完全合理，但当你试图把它们带到现实世界时，它们就瓦解了。说到证据，我会把你引向我最喜欢的两位 Richard。一位做了 Clojure：[VIDEO]，另一位因 Quantum Electrodynamics 获得诺贝尔奖：[LINK]
comments.text: The feeling you're describing is called anxiety. Some anxiety is normal, but constant anxiety that interferes with your life is a problem. I think it'd be worth trying that label on: call it anxiety, and ask "how do I reduce my anxiety?". About 1 in 4 people experience an anxiety disorder at some point in their lives, so there's a lot of research and good approaches out there. One thing that stands out to me is that you've made some pretty big and scary claims without a lot of evidence to back them up. Are you actually not a good developer? Are smart people really "capturing" the opportunity (ie there is less opportunity over time)? Do people who aren't working all the time fall behind and never make anything of significance? If so, prove it! Figure out what evidence you would need to definitively answer these questions, and research or experiment until you have that evidence. Anxious thoughts are like dreams: they seem perfectly reasonable in your head, but when you try to bring them into the real world they fall apart. As far as evidence goes, I'd point you in the direction of two of my favourite Richards. The one who did Clojure: [VIDEO] and the one who got a Nobel for Quantum Electrodynamics: [LINK]

comments.author: greenyouse
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Does being practical act as a hinderance to one’s imagination?
comments.why_zh: 反对围绕生产力进行焦虑式思考的证据。
comments.text_zh: 没人会因为对某件事不确定就是愚蠢的。在思考一个难题时，寻求帮助或意见完全没问题。要回答你的问题，你应该理解创造力和实用性在你的语境中意味着什么。我通常认为，务实和富有创造力并不相互冲突。处理工作中的问题时，我倾向于偏重实用性。我们可能是在想出一种做数据转换的新方法、构建分布式追踪工具，或者尝试一种新的项目脚手架方式。这些都解决了真实问题，并具有实际意义。它们也需要创造性思维来想象和设计新工具与工作流。这些项目之所以务实，是因为它们需要解决一个实际问题（例如，为客户体验或开发速度带来净收益）。与听起来相反，它们往往不是显而易见该接手的项目，也不是直截了当的解决方案。想出其中一个通常需要数天或数周的横向思维。在这个语境下，创造性思维补充了实用性思维，并产生了比单独采用其中一种模式更好的结果。有时，绕着你以为自己想解决的问题转一圈，有助于更好地理解你真正的问题是什么。阅读别人的想法时要小心，因为它会影响你看待问题的方式。读完其他信息后，你对问题的看法可能会被扭曲。O
comments.text: Nobody's stupid because they're not sure about something. It's totally cool to ask for help or opinions when you're thinking through a hard problem. To answer your question you should understand what creativity and practicality mean in your context. I would generally think that being practical and creative aren't at odds with each other. When working through a problem for work I tend to err on the side of practicality. We could be coming up with a new way to do data transformations, building out distributed tracing tools, or trying a new way of scaffolding our projects. Each of those solve a real problem and have practical implications. They also require creative thinking to imagine and design new tools and workflows. These projects are practical in the sense that they need to solve an actual problem (e.g. deliver a net benefit to customer UX or development velocity). Contrary to how they sound, they often aren't obvious projects to take on or straight-forward solutions. It usually required days or weeks of lateral thinking to cook up one of these. In this context, creative thinking complimented practical thinking and produced a better result than one of those modes taken in isolation. Sometimes it's helpful to circle around the problem you think you want to solve to better understand what your actual problem is. Be careful reading other's ideas since it will affect the way in which you see the problem. Your view of the problem may be skewed after reading other information. O

comments.author: rektide
comments.story_title: The Parable of Two Programmers (2012)
comments.why_zh: 在与时间和投入相关的其他投稿中被提到。
comments.text_zh: 真是一个故事。这是一个多么关键的洞见，也是关于世界往往如何运转的一堂核心课程。> 在下一次薪资评审时，Charles 得到的加薪大约是该时期通货膨胀的一半。他没有获得晋升。大约一年后，他变得灰心，离开了 Consolidated。公平地说，对 Alan 而言，从零搭建一个组织和知识体系是非常辛苦的工作。让自己的项目获得正当性也是非常辛苦的工作。但围绕谁来掌舵、工作如何开展，存在如此大的张力；而且有那么多真正优秀、扎实的工作者被漏掉，从未得到赏识。公司这个大机构常常离处在边缘的工作者非常远，看到的是缺点和问题，却无力去赏识和尊重许多为其完成的最佳行动。感谢分享。这是一篇很棒的文章。我看到它与其他投稿有很多关联。Jonathan Blow 谈论工作与生活平衡，在“我们如何用力投入”这一点上与此有一定关联（ [LINK] [LINK] ）。程序员的“中年危机”似乎极为切题（ [LINK] [LINK] , 2 条评论 ）。“Hammock-driven development”也曾流传，并引发反对（ [VIDEO] [LINK] ）。所有这些都涉及时间基准、承诺与投入的问题，所有这些都感觉可以从 The Parable 中获得启发。值得指出的是，据说这则寓言出自（1985）！听到卑微的工程师为完成工作并融入其中而挣扎并非新鲜事，这多少印证了这一点。
comments.text: What a tale. This is such a key insight, such a core lesson on how the world tends to work. > At his next salary review Charles was given a raise which was about half the inflation over the period. He was not given a promotion. After about a year he became discouraged and left Consolidated. To be fair to Alan, spinning up an organization & knowledge system is real hard work. Legitimizing your projects is real hard work. But there's such tension over who steers, over how the work happens, and there's so many really good solid workers who slip through the cracks & never get appreciated. The corporate body is so often so very far away from the workers on the edge, sees the faults and problems, incompetent at appreciating and respecting many of the best acts done for it. Thanks for the share. This is a great article. I see a lot of relationships to other submissions. Jonathan Blow talking about work-life balance has some relationship here, on how we exert ourselves ( [LINK] [LINK] ). The "midlife crisis of a programmer" seems ultra-pertinent ( [LINK] [LINK] , 2 comments). "Hammock-driven development" made the rounds against ( [VIDEO] [LINK] ). All of these deal with questions of time-base & commitment & application, all of these feel like they could be informed by The Parable. Worth pointing out that the parable is reportedly from (1985)! It's somewhat confirming to hear the struggles of the lowly engineer to get work done & fit in are not new.

comments.author: juunpp
comments.story_title: The brain simulates actions and their consequences during REM sleep
comments.why_zh: 把 hammock-driven development 与睡眠中大脑连接想法的现象联系起来。
comments.text_zh: Hammock-driven development 确实存在：[VIDEO] 我觉得任何人都能体会到这一点，哪怕你并不知道背后的科学原理。睡眠中的大脑还能以日常逻辑过程很难做到的方式，把看似不相关的东西连接起来。这就是为什么你睡醒时会觉得某些事情突然“通了”。如果说你白天的思考是梯度下降，那睡眠中的思考就是从所有点、所有方向涌来的洪水。不过这方面我没有任何科学文献可引；只是我的个人经验。
comments.text: Hammock-driven development is a thing: [VIDEO] I think anyone can experience this even if you're unaware of the science behind it. The brain during sleep can also connect seemingly disconnected things in ways that your daily logical process would have a lot of trouble with. That's why things seem to "click" when you wake up from sleep. If your daily thinking is a gradient descent, your sleep thinking is a flood from all points and in all directions. But I don't have any science refs on this; just my experience.
